$comment: STATIC LIBRARY (`ar` archive of relocatable members) for macho64-arm64-darwin. c171 (D-FF1-AR-STATICLIB-DRIVER-WIRING). IDENTICAL to the `macho64-arm64-darwin` relocatable format -- its Mach-O MH_OBJECT arm64 members are written by the SAME relocatable writer + the same sections[]/relocations[] rows -- PLUS exactly `container: "archive"` + `artifactProfiles: ["staticlib"]` + the `-staticlib` name. The archive framing itself is FORMAT-BLIND (src/link/format/ar.cpp): the SysV `.a` armap for ELF/Mach-O, the Microsoft `.lib` 2nd linker member for PE (flavor threaded from kind() in linkAndWriteStaticArchive). No writer code is format-specific to the archive. Kept in sync with the relocatable sibling by hand: any section/reloc change there must mirror here.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this artifact form has NO image header field for a stack size (a relocatable object / static archive is an INPUT to a later link, not a loadable program), so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy -- request the reserve on the build that produces the final EXECUTABLE image -- rather than silently dropped.
$containerComment: D-FF1-AR-STATICLIB-DRIVER-WIRING (c171): `container: archive` marks this as a STATIC-LIBRARY format. The driver (compileOneTarget) dispatches on THIS field -- never the artifactProfile name (the artifact_profile.hpp veto) -- routing each CU's relocatable member (.o) into ONE `ar` archive via linkAndWriteStaticArchive. This is the user's Option-1 format-container decision: output SHAPE stays 100% format-driven (cli->exec, lib->shared, staticlib->archive), exactly as elf.type / pe.type / macho.filetype select the single-file shapes.
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the `staticlib` artifact profile (plan 06). It is the FIRST format to declare it -- the bare relocatable sibling serves NO profile (a `.o` is an internal cross-CU intermediate / a static-archive member, never a project's final artifact). enforceArtifactProfileFormat validates a `staticlib` project against this set. ★ `module` JOINED THIS SET 2026-08-15 (plan 06 §5.1 B.12, as CORRECTED): a module IS a library, so it is served by every format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module` is SourceMerge — a consumer takes its SOURCES and ignores its artifact). Those are orthogonal, so a module builds standalone like any other library and the static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec the author writes in `targets[]`, exactly as it already is for `lib` vs `staticlib` — no new rule and no engine change.
$externCallDispatchComment: D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-CALL-MACHO (closed this cycle): extern FUNCTION calls lower into this relocatable object — a plain BL + BRANCH26 reloc against an SHN_UNDEF-style N_UNDF|N_EXT symbol carrying its REAL import name (the macho.cpp undefined-extern loop now emits `externName`, i.e. the pipeline-mangled `_`-prefixed C name, not the internal `_sym_<id>` — the blocker the #42 note documented). The FINAL linker (ld64/clang) synthesizes the stub/GOT, exactly like the ELF c141 `direct-plt` contract; DSS never builds a stub in a `.o`. The x86_64-darwin object sibling stays leaf-only (no runtime leg exists to witness it — the D-LK1-MACHO-X8664-DARWIN-DATA-SECTION untested-form discipline); its walker code is shared and lights up by declaring this field when a runner lands.
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED + D-LK-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-UNCONSULTED-BY-ELF-AND-MACHO-WRITERS: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. Mach-O puts the weakness in a per-symbol FLAG BIT set ALONGSIDE an ordinary binding: N_WEAK_DEF (0x0080) in the nlist_64's n_desc, on a symbol that is otherwise N_SECT|N_EXT -- the constant re-verified against MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/mach-o/nlist.h. That is exactly what distinguishes `symbol-flag` from ELF's `symbol-binding` (where the weakness IS the binding value) and from COFF's `comdat` (a per-SECTION policy). Written by `definedNDesc` in the MH_OBJECT arm of src/link/format/macho.cpp. THE IMAGE SIBLINGS (exec / dylib) DELIBERATELY DECLARE NO DIALECT, AND THAT IS AN ANSWER RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: their walker encodes no weak definition at all -- refuseWeakImageAlias refuses one outright, because N_WEAK_DEF on an IMAGE additionally needs MH_WEAK_DEFINES in the mach header and those writers copy the schema's flags verbatim (D-LK3-DYLIB-WEAK-EXPORT) -- and a key nobody reads drifts silently while reading as authoritative, which is worse than no key at all. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. The MH_OBJECT arm READS this key and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted. The loader additionally refuses this key at LOAD when the declared dialect is not one the resolved backend's walker writes (ObjectFormatBackend::weakDefinitionDialects).
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: Apple's C ABI prefixes EVERY C symbol with exactly ONE leading underscore, on both 32- and 64-bit Mach-O -- the rule has no bitness axis and no per-arch axis (the arm64 and x86_64 slices of the universal libSystem decorate identically), which is why it is declared per FORMAT and not per target. EVIDENCE, EACH LABELLED. MEASURED-BY-EXECUTION (recorded TF-C113, the macOS cross-build arc): a Windows host cross-emitted a mach-o arm64 binary whose only process-exit path is the `_exit` import, and it RAN on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac and exited correctly -- an undecorated `exit` would have been an unresolved dyld bind, not a cosmetic difference. MEASURED (recorded TF-C121): libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64`, i.e. the C identifier `fstat` reaches the linker as `_fstat`. NOT RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE, stated rather than buried: the Mac is a personal machine and was not declared reachable, so nothing here rests on a probe taken today. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: macOS/Darwin (Apple x86_64 + arm64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation. Apple's enumerated arm64 ABI divergences from generic AAPCS64 are char/wchar_t signedness, long double=double, va_list, the red zone, the stack argument area, and empty-struct handling — NOT bit-field packing — so Mach-O shares gnu_packed (the SAME value the x86_64-darwin object + both darwin exec formats declare).
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: Apple arm64 `long double` IS `double` (64-bit IEEE, 8/8) — a documented Apple divergence from generic AAPCS64's binary128. See macho64-arm64-darwin-exec.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O MH_OBJECT arm, c147 — the macho analog of the ELF c142 `.o` data sections): a relocatable object DOES carry data — a global lands in `__TEXT,__const` / `__DATA,__data` / `__DATA,__bss` / `__DATA,__const` with walker-computed flat-`.o`-space addrs and an N_SECT|N_EXT nlist_64 (n_sect = the section's 1-based ordinal, n_value = the item's FLAT address) the FINAL linker (ld64/clang) binds. Same format-blind `AssembledModule.dataItems` producer path as ELF/PE. D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O arm): a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;` — sqlite's VFS method tables + `aSyscall[]`) lands in `relro` = `__DATA,__const` and the writer emits its OWN relocation_info table (ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED, r_extern=1, addend IN the 8-byte slot bytes — Mach-O's in-place-addend convention; there is no RELA addend column); a reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global lands in `data`. TLS (`tdata`/`tbss`) stays UNDECLARED — the linker's acceptsDataSection gate rejects it loud (the MH_OBJECT walker emits no `__thread_data`/`__thread_vars`; the exec TLV machinery is MH_EXECUTE-only, D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL C4).

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_ARM64 = (12 | CPU_ARCH_ABI64 0x01000000) = 0x0100000C = 16777228 (the SAME value the macho64-arm64-darwin-exec schema declares). cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_ARM64_ALL (0). filetype = MH_OBJECT (1). flags = 8192 = MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS (0x2000), SET 2026-08-20 — see below; this ONE NUMBER is the whole switch and the whole revert. ★ IT IS THE HEADER HALF OF A PAIR, AND THE PAIR IS THE ONLY DISCRIMINATOR MACH-O HAS between a whole file-local (`static`) body and an interior block label: nlist_64 carries no size field, so DSS emitted both as a bare N_SECT with n_desc = 0 and no reader could tell them apart — the archive-member reader classified every `static` function as a label and DROPPED ITS BYTES, loudly when it was called and SILENTLY when it was not (D-LINK-NONEXTERNAL-DEFINED-SYMBOL-READ-AS-BLOCK-LABEL-NOT-ATOM). The per-symbol half is N_ALT_ENTRY (n_desc bit 0x0200), which the writer now stamps on the synthetic per-block labels; this flag is the producer's declaration that every OTHER defined symbol starts an atom of its own. This is the FORMAT's vocabulary, not a DSS convention: ✔MEASURED (operator, real Apple Silicon, 2026-08-20) `/usr/bin/clang -c -O0` sets 0x00002000 on EVERY ordinary `.o`, and ✔MEASURED (this cycle, clang 19 targeting arm64-apple-macos) the same, so an object WITHOUT the flag is the odd one out and cannot be sliced symbol-by-symbol by anyone. ⚠ THE PRIOR TEXT HERE WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW SATISFIED RATHER THAN OVERTURNED: it withheld the flag because the walker emitted a flat `__text` with 'no N_ALT_ENTRY subsection markers', so advertising it 'would lie to ld64 about function-granular dead-strip safety', and deferred the work to plan 14 §3.1 D-LK3-2 — an anchor that closed as the MH_EXECUTE/LC_MAIN row and so had owned this for nobody. The markers now exist; the declaration is honest. ⚠ THE BIT IS A LICENCE, NOT A REQUEST: it permits Apple's ld64 to dead-strip at SYMBOL granularity in every artifact built from these objects, which is why it was gated on hardware evidence rather than on a DSS round trip. ✔MEASURED (operator, real Apple Silicon, 2026-08-20): 38 DSS mach-o objects linked by ld64 under `-dead_strip` with the flag patched ON vs OFF — 38/38 rc=0 both ways, 38/38 ran identically; and a four-variant table (flag on/off × N_ALT_ENTRY on/off), each linked with and without `-dead_strip` — all 8 cells rc=0 with identical correct output. ★ NO C++ READS THIS VALUE: the writer copies `MachOIdentity::flags` verbatim into the header, and the reader asks only whether the bit is present in the object it is READING. So if a widened ld64 sweep ever shows a behaviour change, setting this number back to 0 is the entire rollback — the N_ALT_ENTRY markers stay honest and the reader falls back to its narrower external-only rule with the coverage guard still refusing any dropped body.

$buildVersionComment: D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT, MH_OBJECT arm — and THIS FILE MUST CARRY IT, which is the whole finding. An `ar` archive is not a Mach-O file: the `!<arch>` framing has no load commands and cannot hold a platform declaration, so in a real toolchain the platform lives in each MEMBER, because `ar` merely archives `.o` files that clang already stamped. DSS matches that by construction — `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` (src/program/compile_pipeline.cpp) links every member through the SAME `linker::link` -> `macho::encode` MH_OBJECT walker, handing it THIS schema, not the bare relocatable sibling's. So the walker's `image.buildVersion.has_value()` gate reads THIS file, and omitting the key here would ship an archive whose members each draw `ld: warning: no platform load command found` — the exact defect the sibling closes, surviving inside the `.a`. Members get the emitter for free; they do NOT get the declaration for free. Values are the sibling's verbatim (`macos` / 11.0 / 11.0) under this file's standing 'kept in sync with the relocatable sibling by hand' rule. ⛔ UNRUN, stated rather than implied: no DSS-emitted Mach-O `.a` has been fed to ld64, so the claim here is member-byte emission plus the mechanism above, not archive link acceptance — the same honest boundary this file's `$supportedDataSectionsComment` draws.

sections.$comment: Executable code. Mach-O two-level naming: section `__text` inside segment `__TEXT`. section_64.flags = S_REGULAR (0x0) | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x00000400) = 0x80000400. addrAlign = 16 RAW BYTES (x86_64/arm64 code alignment). section_64.align is a LOG2 exponent and the walker converts (std::countr_zero), exactly as every other section row here is converted; this row used to carry the literal log2 4 and be written VERBATIM, which made one schema key mean two different things across the object and exec families (D-MACHO-TEXT-SECTION-ALIGN-RAW-BYTES-INTO-LOG2-FIELD), written VERBATIM by the walker (the data rows below use the raw-byte-floor convention instead; see their comments). PE's substrate `type` field repurposed for Mach-O section_64.flags. The x86_64-darwin object sibling stays text-only + leaf-only (no runtime leg to witness it); THIS arm64 file carries the data rows (D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE, c147).
sections.name: __text

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O arm, c147): read-only initialized data (string literals, const globals WITHOUT relocations) — exactly where clang places it in an arm64 `.o`: section `__const` inside the R+X `__TEXT` segment. section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = S_REGULAR (0). addrAlign = 8 is the RAW-BYTE alignment FLOOR fed to the shared `buildExecDataSection` substrate (the SAME convention the darwin-exec schema's data rows use); the walker H1-raises it to the strictest member alignment and writes section_64.align as log2 (countr_zero) — UNLIKE the `__text` row above, whose addrAlign is the literal log2 field. No `virtualAddress`: MH_OBJECT section addrs are walker-computed in the flat `.o` address space (text at 0, each next section H1-aligned after the previous), and validate() rejects a non-zero VA on an object row.
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O arm, c147): writable initialized data (mutable globals, `int counter = 7;`) — clang's `__DATA,__data`. section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = S_REGULAR (0). addrAlign = 8 raw-byte floor (H1-raised; walker writes log2 — see the rodata row's comment). A reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global also lands here and the walker emits its relocation_info against this section (r_address = the slot's section-relative offset).
sections.name: __data

sections.$comment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O arm, c147): relocated-read-only const data — a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;`). In an arm64 `.o` clang emits this as `__DATA,__const` — the `.o` PRECURSOR of the image's `__DATA_CONST,__const` (ld64 gathers `__DATA,__const` input sections into the __DATA_CONST segment, read-only after rebase — the Mach-O analog of gcc's `.data.rel.ro` / GNU_RELRO). section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = S_REGULAR (0); the two `__const` rows are DISTINCT Mach-O sections because the (segment, section) PAIR is the identity — (`__TEXT`,`__const`) is the reloc-free rodata row above. addrAlign = 8 raw-byte floor (H1-raised; walker writes log2). The walker emits this section's OWN relocation_info table (the c145 `.rela.data.rel.ro` analog): ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED, r_extern=1, r_length=3, addend written INTO the 8-byte slot (in-place-addend — Mach-O relocation_info has no addend column).
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (Mach-O arm, c147): zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;`) — clang's `__DATA,__bss`. section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = S_ZEROFILL (1): size > 0 but section_64.offset = 0 and NO file bytes (the flat-space addr still advances — LC_SEGMENT_64.vmsize covers it, filesize does NOT). The walker emits it LAST in the section list (the zerofill-last Mach-O convention). addrAlign = 8 raw-byte floor (H1-raised; walker writes log2).
sections.name: __bss

sections.$comment: D-LK-MACHO-COMPACT-UNWIND-SECTION-REFUSED-BLOCKS-EVERY-STOCK-MACOS-ARCHIVE: PER-FUNCTION UNWIND METADATA -- the section Apple's clang emits BY DEFAULT, which is why its absence from this list refused every stock macOS `.a`. ★ THE VOCABULARY IS THE FIX, NOT A GUARD CHANGE: `readRelocatableObject` was right to refuse a section it could not classify, and the linker must never learn the NAME `__compact_unwind` -- it reads the universal `kind`, and the next platform's equivalent section is a row like this one rather than a second branch. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 against Apple clang 21.0.0 (macOS 26.5.2 arm64, `clang -c` with NO flags, `otool -l` + a decoder written from the format description): segment `__LD` / section `__compact_unwind`, section_64.flags (substrate `type`) = 0x02000000 = S_ATTR_DEBUG, section_64.align = 3 (log2) => addrAlign 8 raw-byte floor, and a body of 3 records for 3 functions in 0x60 bytes => entrySize 32 (`{ uint64 functionStart; uint32 length; uint32 encoding; uint64 personality; uint64 lsda; }`). entrySize is READ, not decoration: it is how the reader states HOW MANY function unwind descriptions an object carries without any record layout being hardcoded in C++. ⚠ `__LD` IS A LINKER-ONLY PSEUDO-SEGMENT -- no such segment exists in a linked image, so this row appears ONLY on the relocatable documents and never on an exec or dylib one. ⚠ THIS ROW MAKES DSS READ THE SECTION, NOT CARRY IT, AND THAT IS STILL TRUE OF **THIS** ROW ALONE. D-LK-MERGED-FOREIGN-FUNCTIONS-CARRY-NO-UNWIND-INFO-IN-THE-IMAGE: a compact record is `{fnStart, len, encoding, personality, lsda}` with NO PC DIMENSION, so it describes the frame in the function BODY only. Turning it into an FDE that claims the body rule holds from pcOffset 0 would manufacture an assertion clang never made and be WRONG for every prologue PC -- so it is NOT converted, and the reader says out loud, once per section, which functions reach the image undescribed. Its honest carry is a `__TEXT,__unwind_info` synthesis, which DSS does not yet emit. ★ THE `encoding` KEY IS WHAT LETS THIS ROW COEXIST WITH A SECOND `unwind` ROW: the ROLE (`kind`) is shared, the WIRE ENCODING is not, and the reader dispatches on the declared encoding rather than on this section's NAME. `entrySize` is meaningful HERE and only here -- a compact record is fixed-width, a DWARF CIE/FDE is not.
sections.name: __compact_unwind

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The per-module LINK-TIME-OPTIMIZATION SUMMARY. flags = S_ATTR_DEBUG (0x02000000 = 33554432), which is Mach-O's spelling of non-ALLOC: it is a LINKER INSTRUCTION -- do not load these bytes into the image -- and it is the SAME value the `__LD,__compact_unwind` row already carries for the same reason, reused rather than re-decided. ⚠ IT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THESE BYTES ARE DEBUG INFO, and the distinction is load-bearing: `strip` must not be able to remove the link-time optimizer's input. The `SectionKind` is its own role for exactly that reason. Its OWN SEGMENT `__DSS` -- the `__LLVM,__bitcode` precedent -- so the pair never lands inside a segment ld64 lays out. PAIRED with the `__mir` row below; the SPLIT is the whole economy (see section_kind.hpp).
sections.name: __summary

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-CARRIES-NO-SUMMARY-OR-MIR-SECTION. The module's serialized MIR body -- the LARGE half of the pair, read only for the modules the summary pass selected. Same segment and S_ATTR_DEBUG declaration as the summary row above and for the same reasons; the two differ in PAYLOAD, never in wire treatment.
sections.name: __mir

relocations.$comment: 32-bit PC-relative BL/B branch (call). r_type = ARM64_RELOC_BRANCH26 (2), r_pcrel = 1, r_length = 2 (4 bytes). Mach-O `relocation_info.r_info` packs bits 28..31=r_type, 27=r_extern, 25..26=r_length, 24=r_pcrel, 0..23=r_symbolnum. The MH_OBJECT walker emits the static portion (type+length+pcrel = 0x25000000) from this nativeId and ORs in r_extern + r_symbolnum at emit time. `kind` = 1 matches arm64.target.json's `call26` (the cross-reference the assembler emits + the walker validates). Mach-O has no Rela addend column — addends live in the patch bytes. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_BRANCH26

relocations.$comment: ADRP page-of high-21 (the `adrp` half of an address materialization). r_type = ARM64_RELOC_PAGE21 (3), r_pcrel = 1, r_length = 2 → nativeId = (3<<28)|(2<<25)|(1<<24) = 0x35000000. `kind` = 2 matches arm64.target.json's `adr_prel_pg_hi21`.
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_PAGE21

relocations.$comment: ADD/LDR pageoff low-12 (the `add`/`ldr` half of an address materialization). r_type = ARM64_RELOC_PAGEOFF12 (4), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 2 → nativeId = (4<<28)|(2<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x44000000. `kind` = 3 matches arm64.target.json's `add_abs_lo12_nc`.
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_PAGEOFF12

relocations.$comment: Absolute 64-bit data pointer. r_type = ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED (0), r_pcrel = 0, r_length = 3 (8 bytes) → nativeId = (0<<28)|(3<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x06000000. `kind` = 4 matches arm64.target.json's `abs64`.
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED
